newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Ed delays restart at Fermi 2 nuke.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Ed delays restart at Fermi 2 nuke.

text.p: Detroit Edison will interrupt the restart of its 1,116 megawatt (MW) Fermi 2 nuclear power plant for several days of repairs, the company said Monday.
"We plan to interrupt the operation of the plant and shut down today," spokeswoman Mary Kay Bean said Monday.
The Monroe County, Mich., plant began the restart process on Friday from a 63-day scheduled maintenance and refueling outage which started Sept 27, Bean said.
An electronic problem discovered during restart testing requires shutting down the plant, she said, adding it likely will be shut for "a matter of days."
The unit was operating at about nine percent of capacity as of early Monday afternoon and had not synchronized to the electricity grid, the spokeswoman said.
Detroit Edison, a subisidary of DTE Energy Co, has an overall generating capacity of 10,219 MW.
About 85 percent of the company's generation comes from coal-fired plants, while the rest comes mostly from Fermi 2.
